transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I, um... I hope I'm not wasting your time with this. It's probably just me getting older, or maybe I'm just being a bit scatterbrained lately, but... I just can't seem to keep my mind on one thing anymore. 

I'm a carpenter, and, well, if I'm in the middle of a task and a saw starts up across the shop, or somebody just walks past the office... I completely lose my place. Sometimes even just having a thought about a different job will pull me right off what I’m doing. And before I know it, the whole day just kind of gets away from me. 

Is... is that the sort of thing you help with? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Have you struggled with focus like this since you were a child, or is this a more recent change?

Well, um... I guess if I really think about it, it's not entirely new. I hope it's okay to go this far back, but... even in grade school, like way before I was 12, it was a bit of a struggle. 

I wasn't a bad kid or anything! I really tried to be good and do what I was told. But my teachers, they were always telling my mother that I was... well, they said I was bright, which was really nice of them to say, but they also used the word "careless" a lot. I was always misplacing my homework, or, um, I'd forget the instructions right after they gave them to us. I'd end up just sort of staring out the window instead of finishing my seatwork. 

I think I just had a big imagination, you know? I didn't mean to be a problem for them. But, um... yes, I suppose I've been like this for a long time. Does that answer your question okay? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Aside from feeling scattered, do you find yourself constantly worrying about a lot of different everyday things?

Oh, um... no, not really. I mean, I worry about normal things, I suppose, like making sure my clients are happy with my work, or... or getting things done on time, since I've been so behind lately. But I wouldn't say I'm constantly worrying about everything. I'm actually a pretty easygoing person, most of the time! I hope that's a good thing. I just... I mostly just get frustrated with myself for not being able to stay on track. Is that what you meant, or did you mean something else?
